1948-1.title: The Pan-American Conference arrives through Techo
1948-1.description: In April 1948 the delegates to the Pan-American Conference landed at Techo airport, west of Bogotá, very close to what would later become Ciudad Kennedy.

1959-2.title: Techo airport closes
1959-2.description: Techo airport, in what is now Kennedy, closed when El Dorado International Airport began operating.

1961-3.title: The Techo housing plan is born
1961-3.description: President John F. Kennedy visited Bogotá and, with President Alberto Lleras Camargo, launched the Techo housing program sponsored by the Alliance for Progress. It is usually taken as the birth of the locality.

1963-4.title: From Techo to Ciudad Kennedy
1963-4.description: After John F. Kennedy was assassinated, the residents of the Techo neighborhood themselves decided to call it Ciudad Kennedy in his honor.

1967-5.title: The City Council ratifies the name
1967-5.description: The Bogotá City Council ratified the change of name to Ciudad Kennedy. That project started the urbanization of the locality.

1989-6.title: Waste plant where the library stands today
1989-6.description: EDIS built a waste treatment plant that ran until the company was liquidated in 1993. The El Tintal Library was later built on that site.

1992-7.title: Kennedy becomes a locality
1992-7.description: Kennedy was made a locality by Agreement 2 of 1992 of the Bogotá City Council.

1995-8.title: Patio Bonito and Tintal Central strike
1995-8.description: In late 1995, residents of Patio Bonito and Tintal Central blocked access to Corabastos to demand household utilities, a place in the local development plan and better access roads.

2001-9.title: El Tintal Library opens
2001-9.description: In June 2001 the El Tintal Public Library opened in the Kennedy locality.

2003-10.title: Portal Américas starts running
2003-10.description: Service began at TransMilenio's Portal Américas.

2006-11.title: The library is named after Manuel Zapata Olivella
2006-11.description: Under Agreement 224 of 2006 of the Bogotá City Council, the library was renamed El Tintal Public Library «Manuel Zapata Olivella».
